title: Visualization of Recombinant DNA and Protein Complexes Using Atomic Force Microscopy
protocol: Isolate biomolecules to be imaged and place in a suitable aqueous buffer.
Purify proteins using liquid chromatography, immunoadsorption followed by removal of antibody and pellet, or Profinity eXact purification and tag removal.
Purify DNA molecules using miniprep purification.
Confirm composition and purity of protein samples using SDS-PAGE and western blotting.
Confirm sequence and purity of DNA samples by completing a restriction digest and agarose gel electrophoresis.
Incubate samples in an AFM adsorption buffer to promote adherence of the sample to mica.
Use 10 mM HEPES buffer for protein samples.
Include a divalent cation such as Mg2+ or Ni2+ for DNA samples to promote adsorption to the mica substrate.
A suitable Mg2+-containing buffer for DNA is 10 mM Tris, pH 7.5, and 10 mM NaCl, 2 mM MgCl2.
An alternative Ni2+ buffer is 10 mM HEPES, pH 6.8, and 10 mM NiCl2.
Dilute the sample to a concentration of 5 μg/ml in adsorption buffer.
Gently mix.
Store on ice while the microscope is being prepared.
Place the liquid cell probe holder onto the corresponding cantilever installation docking station.
Locate the long, thick cantilever (referred to as the 'B' cantilever) of the sharp nitride lever (SNL) probe to be used for imaging.
Carefully transfer the SNL probe to the liquid cell probe holder, ensuring that the tip remains upright.
Remove the probe holder from the docking station and examine the cantilever under a light microscope to ensure it is intact and properly seated in the liquid cell probe holder.
Carefully remove the AFM head from the instrument dovetail assembly by tightening the knurled head clamp screw.
Invert the AFM head and firmly push the liquid cell probe holder onto the four pins at the base of the AFM head.
Carefully return the AFM head into the instrument dovetail assembly.
Release the knurled head clamp screw to fasten the AFM head into the instrument.
Locate the cantilever tip using the knobs of the onboard light microscope.
Adjust the illumination if necessary to improve tip identification.
Bring the end of the cantilever tip into close proximity of the crosshairs on the instrument software.
Focus the cantilever tip by adjusting the up and down arrows of the optics controller.
Use slow or medium speed while focusing the optics.
Align the laser to the cantilever tip using the laser adjustment knobs.
Move the adjustment knobs until the red laser dot is inside the white illumination spot.
Trace along the cantilever arm in a zig-zag pattern until the laser is positioned on the cantilever tip.
Center the photodetector by adjusting the photodetector knobs on the AFM head.
Position a freshly cleaved sheet of mica attached to a metal AFM specimen disc on the magnetized sample holder atop the AFM holder plate.
Move the AFM head up by selecting the withdraw icon on the instrument software several times.
Rotate the AFM holder plate so the specimen disc is positioned for the initial imaging.
Ensure the mica substrate is centered under the AFM head.
Move the AFM head down toward the surface of the mica using the focus surface control of the instrument software at medium speed.
Switch to slow Z motor speed when the AFM head is approximately 2 mm above the mica.
Proceed to move the probe closer to the mica substrate surface until distinct features on the mica surface or the tip reflection are in focus.
Toggle between surface and tip reflection focal planes using the "focus on:" icon from the instrument software.
Select the tune icon from the instrument software and tune the cantilever.
Set a 5% peak offset.
Engage the probe onto the mica surface.
Set initial scan size to 10 μm and scan rate to 1 Hz.
Set integral gain to 0.2 and proportional gain to 0.4 initially.
Adjust gains as needed for trace and retrace scans to overlap.
Decrease amplitude setpoint to increase interaction between probe and mica.
Capture complete scan images of the 10 μm field.
Decrease scan size to 5 μm and capture complete image.
Decrease scan size to 1 μm and capture complete image.
Decrease scan size to 0.5 μm and capture complete image.
Adjust gains and scan rate as necessary for each scan size.
Disengage the probe using the disengage icon on the instrument software.
Gently mix the DNA or protein sample prepared in Step 1.
Mix 5 μl of the prepared sample with 45 μl of fresh adsorption buffer (final concentration = 0.5 μg/ml).
Carefully add 50 μl of the biomolecule-containing solution onto the mica surface without moving the probe or AFM head.
Pause for 5 minutes to allow biomolecules in the sample to adhere to the mica surface.
At the conclusion of 5 minutes, pipette an additional 50-100 μl of adsorption buffer into the liquid cell probe holder being careful not to touch the probe.
Form a meniscus in the liquid cell probe holder to allow for AFM tapping mode imaging in fluid.
Readjust the photodetector as necessary.
Realign the laser to the cantilever manually if needed due to diffraction patterns from added sample buffer.
Manually retune the cantilever, if necessary.
Re-engage the probe using the instrument software.
Adjust vertical deflection, integral gain, and proportional gain as necessary.
Increase scan size (500 nm-10 μm) to identify regions of interest.
Zoom-in and reduce scan rate to 0.5 Hz to improve image resolution.
Disengage the probe by selecting withdraw icon on the instrument software several times once imaging is complete.
Ensure sufficient clearance between the AFM head and specimen disc before disassembly of the liquid cell or specimen disc.
Thoroughly rinse the liquid cell probe holder and specimen disc with distilled water to prevent salt crystals from forming as residual adsorption buffer evaporates.
Dry the liquid cell probe holder and specimen disc with compressed air.
